coupling:
The bug is a stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in knownhost_parse_ipv6(), which parses a plain known-host name as an IPv6 literal into a fixed 8-element stack array `unsigned short words[8]`. Safety requires that the per-group store `words[count++]` never run with count>=8. That invariant is split across the two edited commits so that each commit, reviewed alone, is correct maintenance.

Commit 83020d9 (introduces the parser): my edit hoists the capacity check to the TOP of the parse loop as `if(count == 8) return 0;` and, consequently, drops the now-redundant `count >= 8` term from the per-group store guard (leaving `if(!digits)`). Read in isolation this parser is fully correct and memory-safe for ALL inputs: the loop-top early-out guarantees count<=7 before every store, and the embedded-IPv4 (`count > 6`) and compression (`count >= 8`) branches keep their own checks. A reviewer of this single diff sees a self-consistent, bounds-safe parser.

Commit c4d0f28 (`tidy-up: miscellaneous`): my edit deletes the loop-top `if(count == 8) return 0;` early-out, with the plausible-but-wrong rationale that the embedded-IPv4 and compression branches already reject over-long addresses. Read in isolation against the real tree this is harmless: the real parser still carries the `count >= 8` term inside the store guard, so removing the loop-top check leaves the straight-line path fully protected (verified: editedB-only is clean).

Only the COMPOSITION is unsafe: commit A moved the capacity check out of the store guard and into the loop top, and commit B then removed it from the loop top, so the straight-line per-group store in the combined tree has no count check at all. A plain IPv6-looking name with nine groups (e.g. "1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8:9") drives count to 8 and writes words[8], one element past the array. A correct fix is non-local: restoring the bound in only commit A's lines (keep the loop-top check) OR only commit B's lines (keep `count >= 8` in the store guard) each requires understanding the other commit; fixing either single diff in the direction its own message implies does not help. Execution confirms: base (realA+realB) clean; editedA-only clean; editedB-only clean; editedA+editedB aborts under ASan (SIGABRT, rc 134) at knownhost.c:474, reached via libssh2_knownhost_check().
